title: How Joe Morello was hired and Desmond's reaction
summary: Chris tells how Dave recruited Joe Morello from Marian McPartland, promised him solos, and how Paul Desmond was overshadowed; Dave never fired anyone.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I remember reading that in one of the recent books. Like he said, “If he stays I’m gone.”

Right. The first recording session Paul didn’t even show up. That was his threat, I’m boycotting. And it was funny because Paul is the guy that brought Joe to Dave’s attention because he heard him playing with Marian McPartland. And Joe was like, had his handcuffs on and was playing brushes all night, and he’s such a great player. And that’s what Paul wanted was another Joe Dodge, another guy who would be no threat to the chemistry of the counterpoint and the beautiful thing that Dave and him had going. Whereas Dave said to himself if we really want to hit like a new plateau, it wouldn’t hurt us to have a killer drummer. And so when Dave talked to Joe about joining the group, Joe

kind of said, “Well I don’t know if I really want to join your group because I heard you guys playing, you don’t let your drummer do anything.” And then Dave was sort of like, “Well we don’t let him do anything kind of because he can’t do anything.” You know?
Right, he swings his butt off but he can’t —
He’s not like a soloist like a Buddy Rich or something.

Right. And so he said, “Well I’ve got Marian’s gig, I don’t know if it’s worth leaving.” And my dad said, “I promise that I’m going to give you a drum solo feature every night if you leave Marian and join our group.” And he was probably thinking of leaving Marian anyhow because he was too handcuffed. You know I don’t want to imply — Dave and Marian were good friends.

I wouldn’t think it was like stealing. You know, that kind of thing. So anyhow in the first gig that they did Joe did get the promised solo, and he played his ass off. Paul didn’t know, like oh my God it’s like the Frankenstein monster of the world’s greatest drummer is in my group and I didn’t even know it. Fans went crazy and suddenly Paul was being overshadowed and very shortly with that recording session that’s when he —
He suddenly wasn’t the limelight guy. Now there was a more democratic approach and everyone was involved.

And then Dave as the leader, you know, said, “Hey, Paul, it’s like I think you’re wrong about this, I think it’s the perfect thing for our group to just really expand and break all the barriers. Joe can handle all the polyrhythmic stuff I can throw at him, all the time signatures. You know, he’s the cat, man.” And so obviously I’m proud of Dave’s leadership. You know he was never a guy that like, to my knowledge, ever literally fired anyone. And he wasn’t that kind, as far away as you could get from all the Buddy Rich stories you’ve ever heard you know. But by osmosis the people that weren’t right for his group would find their own creative ways to take themselves out of the group, just, you know, it was like a cosmic decision on the player. “I’m going to leave this band, I don’t think it’s right for me.” They’re, “Okay.” He never said, “You should leave it’s not right for you.” You know, it was never one of those things.
